liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bird Song** (3 reviews): Reviewer calls it a great performance; Reviewer calls it a perfect version [4][10][11]
- **Box Of Rain** (2 reviews): Reviewer says by the time it started, they felt at home; Reviewer highlights Donna Jean and Phil's contributions to this song [12][14]
- **The Other One** (2 reviews): Reviewer names it among the highlights, along with Goin' Down The Road; Reviewer calls it magical [3][12]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Reviewer says energy picks up here and it is well played throughout [11]
- **Cumberland Blues** (1 review): Sweet performance, though the recording has a splice early in the song [10]
- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): Reviewer finds the performance tight [10]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): Singled out by this reviewer as one of the show's standout moments [3]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Reviewer praises the Truckin' into The Other One jam [4]

## Setlist highlights

- **Bass And Drum Solo**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [15]
- **Bobby's Bee Story**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]

## The recordings

- **gd72-12-12.sbd.miller.32041.sbeok.flacf** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 169 min; rated 3.8/5 by 10 [1]. Said about its sound: Charlie Miller's version sounds bright and clear throughout, and the reviewer considers it better than the other copy on the site; Group vocal harmonies are unusually in tune throughout, which the reviewer calls the best full-band singing they have heard; Recording has several cuts: Mexicali Blues comes in cut, Cumberland Blues has a small cut, and Half-Step is cut [4][7][11]
- **gd72-12-12.sbd.gorinsky.5802.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 129 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the group singing is exceptionally in tune, among the best full-band vocals they have heard; Johnny B. Goode is only partial in this copy [2][8]

## Around the show

- Reviewer's first rock concert; Jerry, Keith and Bob wore spangled Nudie suits, which he assumed was their usual attire [3]
- Show ended around 2:30 a.m.; streets of San Francisco were deserted afterward, and the crowd was bigger than the previous night [6]
- Bobby sounds hoarse, as if sick, noticeable especially on Sugar Magnolia; Donna's screams drew crowd cheers [9]
- Reviewer heard about the show while working on Haight Street, bought a friend's ticket; opening was sloppy as acid kicked in [12]
- Reviewer says the hall was more crowded than the night before [6]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-12-12.sbd.miller.32041.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard from a 7-inch master reel at 7.5ips half-track, transferred to DAT, then digitized and edited to FLAC; Transferred and edited by Charlie Miller using RME Digiface, Samplitude and Cool Edit Pro [1]
- **gd72-12-12.sbd.gorinsky.5802.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard and Audience Composite [2]. Also: Mixed source: soundboard plus audience recording, taken from DAT and CDR to SHN; seeded by G. Gorinsky [2]
